insight_q01: Q4 2025 generated $1,912,295.82 in completed-sale revenue, the strongest quarter in the dataset -- consistent with the built-in holiday-season seasonality (Nov/Dec are weighted ~35-55% above baseline).
insight_q02: Store #106 leads all 24 stores with $336,698.92 in 2025 revenue, roughly 8% ahead of the next-highest store -- worth understanding whether that's driven by store type, region, or local demand before using it as a template for underperforming stores.
insight_q03: Average transaction value is nearly identical between In-Store ($312.12) and Online ($311.92) -- channel doesn't meaningfully affect basket size here, so channel-mix shifts should be evaluated on cost-to-serve and conversion, not AOV.
insight_q04: 724 loyalty members purchased in November 2025, giving Marketing a concrete, addressable list size for any holiday-season loyalty campaign targeting.
insight_q05: The top 5 best-sellers by units are led by an Accessories item (562 units) but are otherwise dominated by Outdoor Gear (3 of 5 spots) -- Outdoor Gear is punching above its ~16% share of the product catalog in unit velocity.
insight_q06: Electronics is the top-revenue category at $3,163,854.10, despite representing only ~12% of the product catalog -- its high average selling price is doing the work; a unit-volume ranking would likely tell a different story.
insight_q08: Transactions in the West region carry a 4.43% average discount, in line with the other regions -- there's no evidence West is being over-discounted relative to the rest of the chain.
insight_q11: The South region has the highest average transaction value at $313.43, only marginally above the other regions (~$310-312) -- not a large enough gap to be a standalone strategic signal on its own.
insight_q12: Return rates are tightly clustered across store types (5.7%-6.5%), with Flagship stores highest at 6.48% -- close enough that this likely reflects overall product/category mix rather than a store-type-specific service issue.
insight_q17: The top 3 Footwear products by revenue are within 3% of each other ($88.1K-$90.8K) -- a genuinely competitive category rather than one dominated by a single hero SKU.
insight_q19: 38.73% of South-region purchasers are loyalty members, in line with the ~38% loyalty rate in the customer base overall -- the South region isn't under- or over-indexed on loyalty enrollment among buyers.
insight_q20: Credit Card is the dominant payment method at $6.0M (46% of revenue), more than 3x Cash ($1.67M) -- any payment-processing fee renegotiation should prioritize the Credit Card rate given its outsized share.
